full_judgment: 42. The plaintiff after lapse of more than 12 years since the date of institution of the suit by way of amendment sought the relief (b)(I)i.e. declaration that the deeds of October 27, 1969 in the name of Ali Ahmed Khandker and Wali Mohammad Siddiqui were forged, fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiff and thus relief having in fact sought against the recipients of the deeds of October 27, 1969 (Ext.9 and 9 (ka) the said recipients became necessary party in the suit and a such plaintiff was required to implead them in the suit and that having not impleaded them the suit so far the same related to it the validity of the deeds of October 27, 1969 was bad for defect of party since they were necessary parties in presence of whom the relief sought in respect of the deeds of October 27, 1969 were required to be adjudicated. In this connection reference may be made to the decision in the case of Mt. Jahan Ara Begum Vs. Al. Md. Shamsul Hoque reported in 27 DLR (AD) 129 wherein it has been held "The position in law undoubtedly is that in the absence of a necessary party a decree cannot be made in favour of the plaintiff. Of course, the question as to what parties are necessary is often not easy to determine. One test which has been recognized as of great importance is that when in the absence of a party the court cannot give an effective remedy, that party is a necessary party. Besides, in order that a party may be considered a necessary party two conditions must be satisfied, first, that there must be a right to some relief against him in respect of the matter involved in the suit and, second, that his presence should be necessary in order to enable the court effectively and completely to adjudicate upon and settle the question involved in the suit". The learned Counsel for the appellants in support of the contention that because of non-impleading the necessary party against whom the relief was sought by way of seeking declaration that the deeds of October 27, 1969 were forged, fraudulent and not binding upon the plaintiff and thus the recipients of the said deeds became necessary party and they having not been impleaded the suit so far the same relates to the relief (b) (I) was bad for defect of party has referred to the case of Mohar Ali and others Vs. Zafar Ali and others reported in 27 MR, 451 wherein it has been observed "On the question of non-joinder of parties reference may be made to the provisions of Order 1 Rule 13 of the Code of Civil Procedure in which it has been laid down that no objection on the ground of non-joinder of parties shall be given effect to unless it has been taken at the earliest possible opportunity and when such objection has not been so taken, it shall be deemed to have been waived. This question, however, is subject to another legal principle. It is no doubt true that the party to a suit shall not be allowed to agitate the question of non-joinder or misjoinder of parties at a subsequent stage if such a plea has not been taken at the earliest opportunity. But there is also another principle which has received judicial recognition, according to which no court shall pass an in fructuous decree. If it is found on a consideration of the evidence on record that a necessary party has not been impleaded in consequence whereof the decree which may be passed in the suit may be set at naught at the instance of the non-impleaded person, such a decree shall not be passed by a Court".
